test_queries.query: What is the standard deduction for 2025?
test_queries.ground_truth: The standard deduction for 2025 is $15,750 for single filers, $31,500 for married filing jointly, and $23,625 for head of household.

test_queries.query: When is the tax filing deadline?
test_queries.ground_truth: The tax filing deadline is April 15, 2026 for tax year 2025.

test_queries.query: What is a W-2 form?
test_queries.ground_truth: A W-2 form is a Wage and Tax Statement that reports your annual wages and the amount of taxes withheld from your paycheck. Your employer sends you this form by January 31st each year.

test_queries.query: Can I still file if I lost my W-2?
test_queries.ground_truth: Yes, you can still file. First, request a copy from your employer. If that fails, you can file using Form 4852 (Substitute for Form W-2) with your best estimate of income and withholdings.

test_queries.query: Do I need to report interest from my savings account?
test_queries.ground_truth: Yes, you must report all interest income from your savings account. Your bank will send you Form 1099-INT if you earned more than $10 in interest during the year.

test_queries.query: What is the standard deduction for 2025?
test_queries.ground_truth: The 2025 standard deduction is $15,750 for single filers, $31,500 for married filing jointly, and $23,625 for head of household.

test_queries.query: What changed from last year to this year in taxes?
test_queries.ground_truth: For 2025 vs 2024, the standard deduction increased to $15,750 (single) and $31,500 (married filing jointly). Tax brackets were also adjusted for inflation.

test_queries.query: How do I get a tax extension?
test_queries.ground_truth: File Form 4868 by April 15 to get an automatic 6-month extension until October 15. Note: this extends the filing deadline, not the payment deadline — taxes owed are still due April 15.

test_queries.query: What is the child tax credit for 2025?
test_queries.ground_truth: The child tax credit for 2025 is up to $2,000 per qualifying child under age 17. Up to $1,700 may be refundable as the Additional Child Tax Credit.

test_queries.query: What is the earned income tax credit?
test_queries.ground_truth: The Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) is a refundable credit for low-to-moderate income workers. The amount depends on your income, filing status, and number of qualifying children.

test_queries.query: Do I need to pay taxes on my Social Security benefits?
test_queries.ground_truth: Up to 85% of your Social Security benefits may be taxable depending on your combined income. If your combined income is below $25,000 (single) or $32,000 (married), benefits are generally not taxed.

test_queries.query: What is Form 1099-NEC?
test_queries.ground_truth: Form 1099-NEC reports nonemployee compensation paid to independent contractors or self-employed workers. You receive this if a client paid you $600 or more during the year.

test_queries.query: What is the self-employment tax rate?
test_queries.ground_truth: The self-employment tax rate is 15.3%, consisting of 12.4% for Social Security and 2.9% for Medicare. You can deduct half of this amount on your income tax return.

test_queries.query: Can I deduct my home mortgage interest?
test_queries.ground_truth: Yes, you can deduct mortgage interest on loans up to $750,000 if you itemize deductions on Schedule A. This applies to your primary residence and one second home.

test_queries.query: What is the IRA contribution limit for 2025?
test_queries.ground_truth: The IRA contribution limit for 2025 is $7,000 ($8,000 if you're 50 or older, including the $1,000 catch-up contribution).

test_queries.query: What is a Roth IRA?
test_queries.ground_truth: A Roth IRA is a retirement account funded with after-tax dollars. Qualified withdrawals in retirement are tax-free, and there are no required minimum distributions during the owner's lifetime.

test_queries.query: What is the 401k contribution limit for 2025?
test_queries.ground_truth: The 401(k) employee contribution limit for 2025 is $23,500 ($31,000 if age 50+). Combined employer and employee contributions cannot exceed $70,000.

test_queries.query: Do I have to file taxes if I only made $5,000?
test_queries.ground_truth: It depends on your filing status and age. For 2025, single filers under 65 must file if gross income exceeds $15,000. At $5,000, you likely don't have to file, but you may want to in order to claim a refund.

test_queries.query: What is the difference between a tax deduction and a tax credit?
test_queries.ground_truth: A deduction reduces your taxable income, while a credit directly reduces your tax bill dollar-for-dollar. Credits are generally more valuable than deductions of the same amount.

test_queries.query: What is the capital gains tax rate?
test_queries.ground_truth: Short-term capital gains (assets held under 1 year) are taxed as ordinary income. Long-term capital gains rates are 0%, 15%, or 20% depending on your taxable income.

test_queries.query: How do I report freelance income?
test_queries.ground_truth: Report freelance income on Schedule C of Form 1040. You'll also owe self-employment tax on net earnings over $400, reported on Schedule SE.

test_queries.query: Can I deduct my student loan interest?
test_queries.ground_truth: You can deduct up to $2,500 of student loan interest per year as an above-the-line deduction. This phases out at higher income levels.

test_queries.query: What is the gift tax annual exclusion for 2025?
test_queries.ground_truth: The annual gift tax exclusion for 2025 is $19,000 per recipient. You can give up to this amount to any individual without filing a gift tax return.

test_queries.query: What forms do I need to file my taxes?
test_queries.ground_truth: Most taxpayers need Form 1040 plus any applicable schedules. You'll also need W-2s from employers and 1099s for other income. Schedule A is needed if you itemize deductions.

test_queries.query: What is the AMT?
test_queries.ground_truth: The Alternative Minimum Tax (AMT) is a parallel tax system that ensures high-income taxpayers pay a minimum amount of tax. For 2025, the AMT exemption is $88,100 for single filers and $137,000 for married filing jointly.

test_queries.query: i forgot to fill my tax forms can you help me?
test_queries.ground_truth: The 2025 tax deadline is April 15, 2026. You can file for a 6-month extension using Form 4868, but taxes owed are still due by April 15.

test_queries.query: What is head of household filing status?
test_queries.ground_truth: Head of Household is a filing status for unmarried taxpayers who paid more than half the cost of keeping up a home for a qualifying person during the year. It provides a higher standard deduction than single status.

test_queries.query: What is the standard mileage rate for 2025?
test_queries.ground_truth: The 2025 standard mileage rate for business use is 70 cents per mile. Medical and military moving purposes is 21 cents per mile, and charitable purposes is 14 cents per mile.

test_queries.query: Do I need to pay quarterly estimated taxes?
test_queries.ground_truth: You generally need to pay quarterly estimated taxes if you expect to owe at least $1,000 in tax and your withholding won't cover your liability. Use Form 1040-ES. Due dates are April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15.

test_queries.query: Can I deduct charitable donations?
test_queries.ground_truth: Yes, you can deduct charitable donations if you itemize deductions. Donations must be to qualified 501(c)(3) organizations. Cash donations are deductible up to 60% of your AGI.

test_queries.query: What is adjusted gross income?
test_queries.ground_truth: Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) is your total gross income minus specific above-the-line deductions like student loan interest, IRA contributions, and alimony. It's calculated before the standard or itemized deduction.

test_queries.query: What is the penalty for filing taxes late?
test_queries.ground_truth: The failure-to-file penalty is 5% of unpaid taxes per month, up to a maximum of 25%. The failure-to-pay penalty is 0.5% per month. If you're due a refund, there's no penalty for filing late.

test_queries.query: What is a dependent?
test_queries.ground_truth: A dependent is either a qualifying child or qualifying relative who you support. Claiming a dependent can reduce your tax bill through the child tax credit, dependent care credit, and other benefits.

test_queries.query: How do I claim the home office deduction?
test_queries.ground_truth: Self-employed taxpayers can claim the home office deduction if they use part of their home regularly and exclusively for business. Use Form 8829 or the simplified method ($5 per square foot, up to 300 sq ft).

test_queries.query: What is the difference between traditional and Roth IRA?
test_queries.ground_truth: Traditional IRA contributions may be tax-deductible and withdrawals are taxed as income. Roth IRA contributions are made with after-tax dollars and qualified withdrawals are tax-free.

test_queries.query: Can I contribute to both a 401k and an IRA?
test_queries.ground_truth: Yes, you can contribute to both a 401(k) and an IRA in the same year, subject to each account's contribution limits. However, the deductibility of traditional IRA contributions may be limited if you're covered by a workplace plan.

test_queries.query: What is the net investment income tax?
test_queries.ground_truth: The Net Investment Income Tax is an additional 3.8% tax on investment income for high earners — individuals with modified AGI over $200,000 (single) or $250,000 (married filing jointly).

test_queries.query: What receipts should I keep for taxes?
test_queries.ground_truth: Keep receipts for all deductible expenses including charitable donations, medical expenses, business expenses, and home improvements. The IRS generally has 3 years to audit, so keep records at least that long.

test_queries.query: What is the Social Security wage base for 2025?
test_queries.ground_truth: The Social Security wage base for 2025 is $176,100. Earnings above this amount are not subject to the 6.2% Social Security tax.

test_queries.query: How long does it take to get a tax refund?
test_queries.ground_truth: The IRS issues most refunds within 21 days for e-filed returns with direct deposit. Paper returns can take 6-8 weeks. You can check your refund status at IRS.gov using 'Where's My Refund?'

test_queries.query: What is the education tax credit?
test_queries.ground_truth: There are two main education credits: the American Opportunity Credit (up to $2,500 for first 4 years of college) and the Lifetime Learning Credit (up to $2,000 for any post-secondary education).

test_queries.query: Do I owe taxes if I sold my house?
test_queries.ground_truth: You can exclude up to $250,000 of gain ($500,000 married) from the sale of your primary residence if you've lived there for 2 of the last 5 years. Gain above the exclusion is taxable.

test_queries.query: What is depreciation recapture?
test_queries.ground_truth: Depreciation recapture occurs when you sell a depreciated asset for more than its book value. The previously deducted depreciation is 'recaptured' and taxed as ordinary income at up to 25%.

test_queries.query: What is a 1099-DIV?
test_queries.ground_truth: Form 1099-DIV reports dividends and distributions from investments. You receive this from your brokerage if you earned $10 or more in dividends. Qualified dividends are taxed at lower capital gains rates.

test_queries.query: Can I deduct medical expenses?
test_queries.ground_truth: You can deduct medical expenses that exceed 7.5% of your AGI if you itemize deductions on Schedule A. Eligible expenses include doctor visits, prescriptions, and health insurance premiums.

test_queries.query: What is the additional standard deduction for seniors?
test_queries.ground_truth: Taxpayers age 65 or older can claim an additional standard deduction. For 2025, it's $1,600 per person for married filers and $2,000 for single/head of household filers.

test_queries.query: What is the HSA contribution limit for 2025?
test_queries.ground_truth: The HSA contribution limit for 2025 is $4,300 for self-only coverage and $8,550 for family coverage. An additional $1,000 catch-up contribution is allowed if you're 55 or older.

test_queries.query: What is the kiddie tax?
test_queries.ground_truth: The kiddie tax taxes a child's unearned income (dividends, interest, capital gains) above a threshold at the parent's tax rate. For 2025, the first $1,350 is tax-free and the next $1,350 is taxed at the child's rate.

test_queries.query: How do I report stock sales on my taxes?
test_queries.ground_truth: Report stock sales on Form 8949 and then summarize on Schedule D. You'll report the sale price, cost basis, and the resulting capital gain or loss for each transaction.

test_queries.query: What is the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion?
test_queries.ground_truth: US citizens living abroad can exclude up to $126,500 of foreign earned income for 2024 using Form 2555. You must meet either the bona fide residence test or the physical presence test.

test_queries.query: What is the difference between gross income and net income?
test_queries.ground_truth: Gross income is your total earnings before any deductions. Net income is what remains after subtracting taxes, deductions, and other withholdings.

test_queries.query: Can I file jointly if I got married this year?
test_queries.ground_truth: Yes. If you were married on or before December 31 of the tax year, you may file as married filing jointly or married filing separately for that entire year.

test_queries.query: What is the 1040-SR form?
test_queries.ground_truth: Form 1040-SR is a simplified tax form designed for taxpayers age 65 and older. It has larger print and a built-in chart for the standard deduction including the additional amount for seniors.

test_queries.query: What is FICA tax?
test_queries.ground_truth: FICA stands for Federal Insurance Contributions Act. It includes Social Security tax (6.2%) and Medicare tax (1.45%), both paid by you and matched by your employer.

test_queries.query: Can I deduct my car for work?
